findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the write-only DIG removal with the universal AC: either narrow the AC to write/create requests, or enumerate that access_check.py and project_ensures DIG defaults are also removed/scoped so no path issues a DIG request without explicit config.
evidence: access_check.py:72,77,262: `jira_project = ... or "DIG"`
project_ensures.py:50 `_DEFAULT_PROJECT = "DIG"`; _effective_project mirrors Backend.project
Plan step 4: 'Remove the Jira Cloud write-side DIG fallback'
AC: 'no request uses DIG unless DIG was explicitly configured'
findings.finding: The plan removes only the 'Jira Cloud write-side DIG fallback', but the AC asserts the universal 'no request uses DIG unless DIG was explicitly configured'. Multiple other sites DIG-default independently: access_check.py (which issues a live probe request) uses `os.environ.get("JIRA_PROJECT") or "DIG"`, and project_ensures._effective_project/_DEFAULT_PROJECT also substitutes DIG. If only backend.py's write `project` property is changed, a live access-check probe can still target DIG, contradicting the AC.
findings.location: Plan step 4 + AC line 'no request uses DIG unless DIG was explicitly configured'
scenarios: An operator with no explicit JIRA_PROJECT triggers reconcile: write path fails closed, but the access-check probe still queries DIG, so a 'DIG request' still leaves the box.
findings.suggested_fix: Name every DIG-defaulting site (backend.project, access_check.run_access_check, project_ensures._effective_project) and state which ones lose the fallback vs. which legitimately keep a create-time default, so the AC's 'no request uses DIG' claim maps 1:1 to the code.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Tie the live/bounded-live write+push validation to a named acceptance criterion or an explicitly named child ticket, OR document why the verified-fake substitute is faithful to the production Jira/Git boundary for the defaulted write path.
evidence: AC-1: 'Verified-fake Cloud/DC apply plus Git/delivery paths complete with ambient resolvers poisoned...'
Compatibility: 'Until bounded-live validation, a compatibility facade may invoke the legacy write path.'

E5 proxy-validation: a cutover defaulting to a new path validated SOLELY through offline substitute that bypasses the live boundary = MAJOR unless live exercise is deferred to a NAMED child ticket or a documented faithfulness rationale is given.
findings.finding: All acceptance criteria for this write/apply cutover are satisfiable through 'verified-fake Cloud/DC' runs; the live external boundary (real Jira Cloud/DC write, real Git push) is only alluded to via 'Until bounded-live validation' and is not tied to a named acceptance criterion or child ticket. The defaulted write path can close green without ever running against the real boundary as it will in production.
findings.location: Testing (RED -> GREEN) / Acceptance Criteria AC-1 / Compatibility section
scenarios: The verified-fake suite goes green but a scope/credential-projection defect only manifests against the real Jira Cloud write API or real Git remote, so the cutover ships broken while acceptance shows pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an acceptance criterion that exercises the defaulted write/apply path against the real Jira Cloud/DC and Git remote (the 'bounded-live validation' gate), or name the child ticket that owns it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how each child is classified as trusted-same-capability / owning / unrelated-sibling and from what source (e.g. adapter capability declaration in the registry).
evidence: 'trusted same-capability children start from ambient inheritance, owning children receive their adapter overlay, unrelated siblings remove exact secret names declared by other Rebar adapters'
The projection outcome depends on a per-child classification whose source/derivation is unstated (signal 1: undefined scope boundary for the classification input).
findings.finding: The child-environment builder classifies children into 'trusted same-capability', 'owning', and 'unrelated sibling' buckets with different projection behavior, but the plan never states how a child is classified into a bucket or from what source that classification is derived.
scenarios: An executor must decide whether a given child process is 'trusted same-capability' vs 'unrelated sibling' and has no stated rule to apply.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the child-env projection contract and adapter secret-name registry semantics in an ADR/AGENTS.md/design-doc so future adapter authors register names correctly.
evidence: 'Add src/rebar/_child_env.py with a pure environment projection API and a checked-in registry of exact secret names owned by each Rebar adapter.'

No plan item records the projection contract, child-classification semantics, or registry maintenance rules in a design doc/ADR; absent such capture, future adapter authors have no reference for what to register.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new cross-component contract (the environment projection API and a checked-in registry of adapter-owned secret names) but does not capture this novel architectural decision in an ADR/AGENTS.md/design-doc update.
scenarios: A new adapter is added later; its author must register owned secret names but has no documented contract for the registry or projection semantics.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that removing the write-side DIG default is compensated by a pre-mutation explicit-scope check that fails closed BEFORE any create (preserving bug-4fa9's guarantee that CREATE never fires without a project), and reference the 4fa9 constraint explicitly.
evidence: backend.py:185-190: 'Effective write/create project, DIG-defaulted to match the create client (bug 4fa9)'
acli_subprocess.py:110-111: 'project_default substitutes for an empty project (e.g. "DIG", which ACLI requires on CREATE — bug 4fa9)'
Plan step 4 removes the fallback but does not restate the create-time project requirement
findings.finding: The plan removes the write-side DIG default but does not address the CREATE-scope constraint that default was introduced to satisfy (bug 4fa9: ACLI requires a project on CREATE). Removing the fallback re-opens the failure mode 4fa9 closed unless the plan states that an explicitly-configured write scope supplies the create project.
findings.location: Plan step 4 / Outcome ('Missing explicit write scope fails before mutation')
scenarios: A create mutation runs with explicit non-DIG scope: works. A create runs with no scope: must fail before mutation (intended), but the plan doesn't confirm the fail-closed path replaces the ACLI-requires-project guard rather than crashing mid-create.
